title: Najlepszy · od + dopełniacz
note: Completes a1_comparatives. Half 1: naj- over that unit's closed set of nine (lepszy, gorszy, wiekszy, mniejszy, starszy, mlodszy, droszy, tanszy, nowszy) - one prefix, no stem change, no exceptions, deliberately framed as the easy unit after gen_pl and aspect. Half 2: the od+Gen comparison a1_comparatives deferred, taught as a free CHOICE against niz rather than a second thing to master. GENITIVE FORMS ARE THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK: every noun after od uses a genitive already taught - herbaty/kawy/domu/miasta/piwa (a1_gen_endings), matki (a1_gen_ki), brata/psa/kota (a1_miec, masculine animate, where accusative and genitive are the same form and the intro says so). Rejected after checking the pool: od mamy (mamy is taught ONLY as the verb 'we have' - the genitive of mama is untaught and the homograph would mislead), od taty (untaught), od siostry (untaught). Also refused as unsafe homographs: corki, wina, gazety, okna, gory - all taught as nominative plurals in a2_plural_nom / a2_travel, not as genitives. Fenced and never on screen: adverb comparison (lepiej, wiecej, najlepiej), najbardziej + adjective, comparative of adverbs, any superlative outside the inherited nine.

intro.title: One prefix. That is the whole rule.
intro.body:
You already have the comparatives: lepszy (better), większy (bigger), starszy (older).

To say the best, the biggest, the oldest, put naj- on the front. Nothing else changes — no new ending, no stem change, no exceptions, no list of awkward ones to memorise.

lepszy → najlepszy · większy → największy · starszy → najstarszy

After the genitive plural and the aspect pairs, you have earned an easy one. This is the cleanest rule in the language so far, and it is worth saying plainly: there is nothing else to learn here.
intro.body_pl: Stopień najwyższy: naj- + stopień wyższy. Bez wyjątków.

intro.title: All nine, built the same way
It agrees like any adjective
intro.body: The superlative changes its ending for the noun exactly as the comparative already does: -y for masculine, -a for feminine, -e for neuter. The naj- never changes.
intro.body_pl: Końcówka jak w stopniu wyższym: -y / -a / -e. Naj- zostaje bez zmian.

intro.title: Two ways to say than — pick either
intro.body:
You already have one way: niż + the dictionary form.

Tata jest starszy niż brat.

Polish has a second way that means exactly the same thing: od + the genitive.

Tata jest starszy od brata.

Same meaning, same register, both completely normal. The only difference is what happens to the second noun. After niż it does not change at all. After od it goes into the genitive — the case you already use after do, z, blisko and dużo.

Use whichever you find easier. Polish speakers use both, and you cannot get this choice wrong.
intro.body_pl: niż + mianownik = od + dopełniacz. To samo znaczenie. Wybierasz sam.

examples.en: The cat is smaller than the dog.
examples.pl: Kot jest mniejszy niż pies. = Kot jest mniejszy od psa.
Kawa jest lepsza niż herbata. = Kawa jest lepsza od herbaty.

examples.en: The city is bigger than the house.
examples.pl: Miasto jest większe niż dom. = Miasto jest większe od domu.

intro.title: The genitive after od — all of it is old news
intro.body:
No new endings. Every form below is one you have already written after do, z, blisko or nie ma.

The last three are a man and two animals. Masculine nouns for people and animals take -a in the genitive: brata, psa, kota. That is the same form you already write after mam — Mam brata. Mam psa.
intro.body_pl: Po od zawsze dopełniacz — te same formy co po do, z, blisko.

quiz.explain: naj- is a prefix, not a separate word — it is written joined onto the comparative with no space and nothing else changes.
The superlative is built on the comparative większy, never on the plain adjective duży — which is why najduży does not exist.
Zły has an irregular comparative gorszy, and the superlative is built on that, so the irregularity is already paid for.
Kawa is feminine, so the ending is -a. The prefix naj- takes no part in the agreement.
Miasto is neuter, so the ending is -e — the same ending you already put on większe.

quiz.prompt: Same meaning as: Tata jest starszy niż brat.
quiz.explain: od hands the genitive to the noun after it, exactly as do and z do. niż does the opposite and leaves the noun alone — so niż brata is wrong for the same reason od brat is.
Pies is the dictionary form, which is what niż would take. After od you need the genitive, and masculine animals take -a.
The same genitive you already write after nie ma and dużo — herbata loses its -a and takes -y.
Matka ends in -ka, and Polish never writes y after k, so the genitive ending is spelled -i.

quiz.prompt: Fix: Miasto jest większe od dom. →
quiz.explain: Dom is the dictionary form and only niż accepts that. After od the masculine genitive is domu — the same word you already use in do domu.

type_items.explain: Brat is masculine and animate, so its genitive is brata — the form you already write after mam.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: This film is the worst.
Type: My sister is the youngest.
Type: The city is the biggest.
Type: The cat is smaller than the dog. (niż or od — both are right)
use_items.explain: Both versions are ordinary Polish. niż leaves pies in its dictionary form; od pushes it into the genitive, psa.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Dad is older than the brother. (niż or od — both are right)
Type: Coffee is better than tea. (niż or od — both are right)
Type: Tea is cheaper than coffee. (niż or od — both are right)
Type: The city is bigger than the house. (niż or od — both are right)
Type: Wine is more expensive than beer. (niż or od — both are right)
Type: The sister is younger than the mother. (niż or od — both are right)
use_items.explain: Matka takes -i rather than -y in the genitive only because Polish never writes y after k. The rule for od is the same for every noun.
